subject: Pilot runway: Tempo Shield (burst insurance) vs 90-day slab — amendment options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara@lumina.ai>, Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@luminalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway: Tempo Shield (burst insurance) vs 90-day slab — amendment options

Hi Sara / Ben,

Good meeting earlier 11 thanks for walking us through the load test details. We discussed two pragmatic approaches to keep your pilot running while procurement evaluates longer-term packaging:

Tempo Shield (short-term burst insurance) - recommended for speed:
- 150k token insurance pool valid for 30 days (covers priority routing and reserved capacity).
- One-time fee: $5,000.
- No automatic overage; if consumption exceeds the pool we fall back to PAYG at $0.032/1k tokens unless you authorize additional bursts.
- Includes one 1-hour tuning session with our infra team.

90-day Prepay Slab (cost-efficient runway):
- 450k token slab applied over 90 days.
- Effective unit price ~20% below standard PAYG for slab consumption.
- Price: $16,000 upfront. Unused slab rolls into a 90-day buffer.
- If you convert to a Dedicated commit within 90 days, we will convert unused slab pro-rata as credit toward the commit (no cash refunds).

Quick trade-offs: Tempo Shield = smallest procurement friction and lowest cash outlay; Slab = better economics but needs Finance sign-off. Both include a temporary pilot SLA uplift (details below) and the engineering hour.

Proposed pilot uplift SLA (short window): p99 <= 240ms; if p99 > 500ms twice in the 30-day window, customer receives a one-time service credit equal to 5% of the pilot monthly spend. Legal will formalize.

Attached: draft amendment (tempo-shield-amendment-draft.docx) with the two options and our usage spike log from today's test run. Please tell us which path you want to move on by Monday EOD and well turn around the signed amendment quickly. Happy to do a split (small slab + shield) if that helps procurement.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Commercial GTM
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs:

From: Sara Li <sara@lumina.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@luminalabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway: Tempo Shield (burst insurance) vs 90-day slab  amendment options

Vivek 

Appreciate the clear options. A couple of procurement questions before we pick:
1) For Tempo Shield, if we see multiple spikes across several days (sustained but intermittent), will Redwood require written approval each time we breach the 150k pool, or can we set an automated overflow throttle at PAYG? We want to avoid manual approvals if possible.
2) For the 90-day slab, procurement is wary of prepay sunk costs. The conversion-credit-to-dedicated path helps. Would you consider a 60-day refund window (pro-rated) if we demonstrably haven't used >30% of the slab after 60 days?
3) Can you circulate the SLA uplift text so our security/compliance and procurement teams can review quickly?

If Tempo Shield can be set to auto-overflow at PAYG unless we opt out, we can greenlight it this week and circle back on slab.

Ben and I are swapping notes on timelines procurement is on a tight cycle this week.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of ML Ops
Lumina Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot runway: Tempo Shield (burst insurance) vs 90-day slab  amendment options

Internal note / suggested response to Sara:
- Tempo Shield: ops can enable automatic overflow to PAYG with an opt-out flag. We'll include explicit language that overflow billable consumption is PAYG at $0.032/1k tokens and that Redwood will email an alert on first overflow event above 10k tokens. This reduces manual approvals and matches customer ask.
- 90-day slab: legal/finance won't do cash refunds. We can offer a conditional 60-day consumption review that, if they haven't consumed >30% by day 60, allows a one-time reassign of the remaining slab as a credit toward a future annual commit or Dedicated conversion (still no refunds). This is our compromise to reduce procurement risk.
- SLA uplift: confirm p99 240ms target; credit formula of 5% applies if p99 exceeds 500ms more than twice in the 30-day pilot extension. Legal will draft precise wording.

Pricing notes: tempo-shield margin ~46% (good quick path), slab margin ~34% but increases chance of commit; happy to offer a modest additional 2% off the slab price if they sign a 12-month commit after conversion within 45 days.

I'll draft an updated amendment reflecting auto-overflow, the conversion-credit mechanics, and the SLA language. Vivek  can you approve routing to Legal after I clean it up?

Marissa
Senior Director, GTM Deals
Redwood Inference
